clue.text: One entering college hashed 28

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 28 across, used for its letters

explanation.surface: A new student arrives at college in a hurried, jumbled state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 28 is a cross-reference: take the letters of COURT-MARTIAL and rearrange them to get MATRICULATOR; 28 is in turn the same trick run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To matriculate is to enrol formally at a university, so the person doing so is someone being admitted to a college.

clue.text: Hampshire town picked up Eastender's transfer

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so what matters is how the words are spoken

parts.note: a transfer is a handing over, and a Cockney East Ender drops the initial H when saying it

explanation.surface: A soap-opera character is transferred to a small town in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: East Enders (people from London's East End, and the TV soap EastEnders) stereotypically drop their initial H, so 'hand over' comes out as 'and over'. Andover is a town in Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Andover is a market town in the English county of Hampshire, so the clue simply names its location.

clue.text: Ceremonial followed by head, old and slowing down

parts.note: a ceremonial is a rite
nut is slang for the head
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned ceremony led by an elderly chief moves slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ceremonial' reads as an adjective but here it is a noun, a formal ritual. RITENUTO is an Italian musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, ritenuto instructs players to hold back the tempo immediately, an Italian performance marking for reduced speed.

clue.text: Will one fix score on pitch? Au contraire

definitions.text: Will one fix score on pitch?
definitions.meaning: surface reading: someone rigging the result of a match played on a sports field
setter's reading: swap it round, and a musical symbol fixes the pitch of notes on a written score

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a football match's result will be rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' and 'pitch' sound like sport; 'Au contraire' tells you to reverse them, making both musical words: the sign fixes pitch on the score.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a stave that fixes which notes the lines stand for, determining their pitch.

clue.text: Guide had time to demote leader when cutting allowance

indicators.note: something cutting into another thing sits inside it, splitting it in two
demoting the leader sends the front letter down to the back of the queue

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
leeway is an allowance or margin of freedom

explanation.surface: A tour guide had time to push a group leader down the ranks while trimming their expenses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demote leader' applies to the joined letters of 'had time', not to any person: the front letter moves to the back. 'Leader' is not a definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide people is to go in front and show them the route, which is exactly what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Giant trip train regularly offers

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken and the rest skipped

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: A huge train journey is offered on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' seems to say how often trains run, but it picks every other letter from the two words beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were enormous deities of Greek myth, so the word is used for any person or thing of great size.

clue.text: Metal layer, one with unusual casing

indicators.note: a casing wraps around its contents, so one part encloses the others

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or unusual
a hen is a bird that lays eggs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A coat of metal is described as having an odd outer shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' suggests a coating of metal, but it is something that lays eggs. RUM as 'strange' is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenium is a rare, dense chemical element, element number 75, classed among the transition metals.

clue.text: Worried 9 panics, perhaps

indicators.note: something worried is agitated and shaken about, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the answer to 9 down, used for its letters

explanation.surface: Anxious music students at a conservatoire keep panicking.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 points at CONSERVATOIRE, whose thirteen letters rearrange to make this answer; 9 uses the same letters the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A panic is one example of reacting far more strongly than a situation warrants, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: 8 worked in a special school

indicators.note: worked material has been kneaded and reshaped, so the letters take a new form

parts.note: the answer to 8 down, used for its letters

explanation.surface: Someone's panics were dealt with at a special school.
explanation.walkthrough: The 8 points at OVERREACTIONS, whose letters rearrange to give this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatoire is a college devoted to training musicians, a specialist institution rather than a general one.

clue.text: Duty reported by extremely valuable sentry

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

indicators.note: something reported is spoken out, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: a duty is something owed, a debt; the French spelling dette is said the same way

explanation.surface: A guard whose duty is reported as extremely valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duty reported' comes first in the clue but its letters go second: 'by' places them beside the ends of 'valuable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vedette is a mounted soldier posted ahead of the lines as a lookout, a military term for a watchman.

clue.text: Style shown by little boy Oscar after one month

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it in the sequence

parts.note: Art is a short form of the boy's name Arthur
DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A small boy called Oscar shows off his fashion sense after a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little boy' asks for a shortened boy's name. Oscar follows the month, so O comes after DEC.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative movement of the 1920s and 1930s, a design fashion in buildings and objects.

clue.text: Compelled to abandon daughter in split

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: someone compelled to act is driven
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent forced to leave their daughter during a separation.
explanation.walkthrough: Take D out of DRIVEN. 'Split' reads as a noun, a family break-up, but it is a past participle, matching RIVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Riven is the old past participle of rive, meaning torn or cleft apart, as a split thing has been.

clue.text: Implements silent manoeuvres in America

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States of America

indicators.note: manoeuvres move things about into new positions, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone carries out secret military manoeuvres in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implements' looks like a verb, carries out, but it is the plural noun: tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Utensils are tools or instruments, especially for the kitchen, so they are implements in the noun sense.

clue.text: Footballer indicating where Spain meets France?

parts.note: surface reading: a geography question about the Pyrenean border between two countries; setter's reading: the international codes E and F sit side by side, and the answer read as an instruction says where that pair goes: into a four-letter direction word

explanation.surface: A footballer points out the border between Spain and France.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a cryptic instruction: E (Spain) and F (France) meet as EF, which sits inside LEFT. An inside left was an old attacking position in football.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside left was a forward position in the traditional football formation, and the term also names the player filling it.

clue.text: It offers submarine training to the UK

definitions.text: It offers submarine training to the UK

parts.words: It offers submarine training to the UK
parts.note: surface reading: a naval establishment that teaches sailors to crew submarines; setter's reading: submarine means under the sea, and training means a train service, crossing to Britain

explanation.surface: An organisation provides submarine instruction to Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' is split as train-ing, running trains, and 'submarine' is taken literally as below the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurotunnel operates the Channel Tunnel, running rail shuttles beneath the sea between France and England.

clue.text: European space station, one over parts of Asia?

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European
Mir was the Soviet and Russian space station

explanation.surface: A European space station orbits over parts of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over' looks like orbiting overhead; it means a person ruling over territory. The question mark flags that this is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander, found in the Middle East, so a person in authority over lands.

clue.text: Dejected players not running up-front

indicators.note: in a down entry, up front means placed at the top, ahead of the other part

parts.note: a system that is down is not running
the players in a production are its cast

explanation.surface: Dispirited footballers who won't run up front for the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' and 'up-front' conjure a football team's forwards; the players are actors, and 'up-front' only positions DOWN first.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means low in spirits, with eyes lowered, so it is a close synonym for someone disheartened.

clue.text: Frank's opposite starts to come and go? Yes

indicators.note: the start of each word is its opening letter, so only those are kept

parts.note: the first letters of four words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Frank's opposite number comes and goes, and gets a yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank means speaking openly, while cagy means guarded and evasive, so the two are antonyms.

clue.text: Go on about endless deception of the corporation?

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to gas is to talk on and on
a trick is a deception

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the ongoing deceit of a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old jocular word for a pot belly, so 'of the corporation' means of the stomach; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric means relating to the stomach, and a corporation is humorous old slang for a large paunch.

clue.text: About to welcome ordinary boy — first fix a drink

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one part holds another
what comes first is placed at the front of the sequence

parts.note: to pin is to fix in place
taken as written
CA is short for circa, about
O is the abbreviation for ordinary
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone about to greet an ordinary lad fixes a drink for him first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' says the pieces fix and a go at the front; then CA holds O and LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A piña colada is a cocktail of rum, pineapple juice and coconut, so it is a particular alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Harpo Marx's half-broken jar

indicators.note: half of a word means only part of it survives, the rest removed
something broken is smashed into pieces that can be put together differently

parts.note: taken as written
its first half: the opening two of its four letters, the rest deleted

explanation.surface: One of the Marx Brothers owns a jar that is half broken.
explanation.walkthrough: Harpo Marx was the silent, harp-playing member of the Marx Brothers comedy team; 'half-broken' splits into two separate instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled ancient Greek or Roman vessel for storing wine or oil.

clue.text: During spring, heart of bride sank in an extreme way

parts.note: during something is in it
a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the letters in the very middle are kept

parts.note: the central three of these nine letters

explanation.surface: In springtime a bride's heart sinks dramatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of bride' seems to point at the middle of one word, but the heart is taken from the two words 'bride sank' together. 'Spring' is a water source, not a season.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom in spades means to a great degree or abundantly, an informal phrase for intensely.

clue.text: Stamp gold rings for so long

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one part surrounds the other

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a stamp for impressing designs on coins

explanation.surface: A gold stamp used on rings for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings' looks like jewellery, but it is a verb: the gold goes round the stamp. 'So long' is a phrase, not a duration.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French farewell also used in English, matching the casual phrase used when parting company.

clue.text: Kill number two following an upset

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this part is placed second
something upset is turned over, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: taken as written
number two is a childish euphemism for poo

explanation.surface: A second-in-command commits murder after being upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number two' suggests a deputy, but it is nursery talk for a bowel movement. NAPOO is First World War army slang.
explanation.definitionFit: British soldiers in the First World War took 'napoo' from French 'il n'y en a plus' and used it to mean finish off or destroy.

clue.text: Watch team getting oddly dismissed in minutes

indicators.note: sending off the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones behind

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Spectators watch a team being strangely sent off within minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' sounds like time on a match clock; it is the written record of a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta is a Latin plural for recorded proceedings or official records, the formal written account of what happened.

clue.text: Priest and old lady returning bong

indicators.note: returning means going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Old Testament book of Samuel
an old lady may be called gran

explanation.surface: A clergyman and an elderly woman come home with a cannabis pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bong' looks like the sound of a bell but is a water pipe. Eli is the crossword's favourite biblical priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A nargile is a Middle Eastern hookah, a water pipe in which smoke is cooled by bubbling through liquid.

clue.text: Constant love for French people's outrage

parts.note: c is the symbol for the constant speed of light
l'amour is French for love

explanation.surface: A steadfast love of the French prompts public anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constant' seems to describe the love, but it is a physics constant, the letter used for the speed of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamour is a loud public outcry or protest, the noisy expression of collective indignation.

clue.text: Perhaps try private rendition of 1

indicators.note: a rendition is a performer's own version, so the letters are rendered in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 1 across, used for its letters

explanation.surface: An attempt to give a private performance of an earlier piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' reads as attempt and 'private' as secluded, but they mean put on trial and a low-ranking soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A court-martial is a military tribunal, so to court-martial a private is one example of putting someone on trial.
